title: What Thailand's Maya Bay teaches us about the missing link in blue finance
gist: Using Thailand's Maya Bay closure and recovery as a hook, World Bank and IFC authors argue blue finance is underfunded relative to the ocean economy's value: SDG 14 gets under 1% of SDG finance and blue bonds are only ~0.25% of a US$6 trillion sustainable bond market, with SABESP, Morocco aquaculture and Pacific tuna cited as investable models.

insights.claim: Before its 2018 closure, Thailand's Maya Bay received about 5,000 visitors and 200 anchoring boats a day, and its national park earned 555 million baht (about US$16 million) in a single season while 50-80% of surrounding coral reefs were damaged.
insights.so_what: Overtourism can destroy the asset generating the revenue; capped access may be the sustainable model.
insights.locator: A few years ago, Maya Bay
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: After Thailand closed Maya Bay in 2018, coral regrew and blacktip reef sharks returned; it reopened in 2022 with capped visitor numbers and stronger management.
insights.so_what: Shows ecosystems can recover quickly when governments accept short-term tourism revenue losses.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The ocean economy generated US$2.6 trillion in value added in 2020, with more than three-quarters of its growth since 1995 coming from Asia and the Pacific.
insights.so_what: Asia-Pacific is the center of gravity for ocean-economy growth and blue investment.
insights.quote: The ocean economy alone generated US$2.6 trillion in value added in 2020, and more than three-quarters of its growth since 1995 came from Asia and the Pacific.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Coral reefs reduce annual expected flood damage by more than US$4 billion globally, and without reefs damage from a one-in-100-year storm could rise by 91%.
insights.so_what: Reef loss directly raises coastal property and insurance losses.
insights.quote: Without reefs, damage from a one-in-100-year storm could rise by 91 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Hotels, dive operators, ports, utilities, coastal property owners and their insurers all lose when marine assets degrade, yet only a small share of the value they derive flows back to maintaining those assets.
insights.so_what: Points to future levies or payment-for-ecosystem-services schemes on coastal businesses and insurers.
insights.quote: economies depend on these assets, but only a small share of that value finds its way back to the assets that make it possible.
insights.locator: The result is a familiar disconnect
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The blue economy could be worth an estimated US$5.5 trillion a year by 2050, yet SDG 14 (life below water) is the least-funded of all 17 SDGs, receiving less than 1% of total SDG finance.
insights.so_what: Large mismatch between economic value and capital allocated signals an underdeveloped asset class.
insights.quote: remains the least-funded of all 17 SDGs, receiving less than 1 percent of total SDG finance.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: In developing countries roughly 91% of water spending comes from the public sector and less than 2% from the private sector, and much of the public spending is off-budget and invisible to finance ministers.
insights.so_what: Water infrastructure in EMs is a near-untapped private investment market.
insights.quote: roughly 91 percent of spending in developing countries comes from the public sector and less than 2 percent from the private sector.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Global blue bond issuance surpassed US$15 billion by mid-2025 but represents only about 0.25% of the sustainable bond market, which exceeded US$6 trillion in cumulative issuance by March 2025.
insights.so_what: Blue bonds remain a tiny niche with room to scale within ESG fixed income.
insights.quote: blue bonds account for only around 0.25 percent of the global sustainable bond market
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Economic value from natural assets does not automatically create investable opportunities; private capital needs clear revenue streams, manageable risks and replicable structures.
insights.so_what: Bankable blue deals require revenue-linked structures, not environmental value alone.
insights.quote: Economic value does not automatically translate into an investable opportunity.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Asia and the Pacific will need about US$53 billion a year for water and sanitation alone through 2030.
insights.so_what: Sizes a large regional water-infrastructure financing need.
insights.quote: Asia and the Pacific will need about US$53 billion a year for water and sanitation alone through 2030.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Morocco's sustainable aquaculture sector, including climate-resilient seaweed, is expected to reach 300,000 tons of production and create 30,000 jobs over the next decade.
insights.so_what: Emerging aquaculture opportunity in North Africa for private investors.
insights.quote: The sector is expected to reach 300,000 tons of production and create 30,000 jobs over the next decade.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Aquaculture is projected to become a US$1.5 trillion investment opportunity globally by 2050.
insights.so_what: Aquaculture is a large long-term growth theme for food and agri investors.
insights.quote: aquaculture is projected to become a US$1.5 trillion investment opportunity globally by 2050.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: SABESP, São Paulo's private water utility, mobilized financing from seven international commercial banks for wastewater collection and treatment in the Tietê River basin under the Integra Tietê program serving over 20 million people.
insights.so_what: Shows commercial banks will lend to water projects with clear revenue streams; positive for privatized utilities like SABESP.
insights.quote: SABESP's blue-finance program mobilized financing from seven international commercial banks
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Through the Parties to the Nauru Agreement, Pacific tuna revenues rose from about US$60 million in 2010 to around US$500 million annually, with industry employment up 44% between 2015 and 2022.
insights.so_what: Collective resource management and science-based limits can multiply resource rents for small states.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: IFC's Beacon for Blue (B4Blue) applies a market-creation approach across water, plastics, aquaculture and shipping in Asia-Pacific to address gaps in standards, project pipelines, capacity and market intelligence.
insights.so_what: Multilateral push to standardize blue finance may expand deal flow for private co-investors.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
